title: Decoupling 2D translation-invariant topological CSS codes
abstract: Two-dimensional translation-invariant topological CSS codes on qubits are known to be locally equivalent, after coarse-graining, to stacks of toric codes. However, existing constructions generally break more translation symmetry than is required to remove anyon-permuting translations, leaving open whether any further obstruction exists. We prove that no such obstruction occurs: after passing to the maximal anyon-preserving superlattice, every such code admits a local unitary decoupling into toric codes and product states. We further provide an efficient algorithm for explicitly constructing the decoupling map, together with bounds on the required supercell size and operator spreading. The decoupling requires no additional ancillas in generic cases and extends to finite systems with suitable boundary conditions.

bite.hook: Proved 2D translation-invariant topological CSS codes fully decouple into toric codes without extra ancillas.
tldr: Investigated 2D translation-invariant topological CSS quantum error-correcting codes on qubits.
Built an efficient explicit algorithm to construct local unitary decoupling maps on maximal superlattices.
Proved that all such codes decouple into toric codes and product states without needing extra ancillas.
bite.whyItMatters: Quantum computers need error-correcting codes to protect delicate quantum bits from environmental noise. Proving that complex 2D codes decompose into simple toric codes simplifies the architecture needed to build reliable quantum memories.
bite.eli5: Imagine discovering a complex modular structure protecting fragile glass. This math proof shows every such structure can be cleanly taken apart into simple, standard LEGO blocks without needing temporary scaffolding. This makes designing safe quantum storage much simpler.
